correctness.rationale: In the five-point blow-up model the 16 exceptional curves have pairwise intersection numbers 0 or 1, and the incidence graph is triangle-free. In particular a meeting is transverse and no point lies on three curves. Label the conic transform by the empty set, E_i by the complement of {i}, and the joining line L_ij by {i,j}; adjacency is then symmetric-difference size four. Coordinate permutations respect these labels, and the root reflection in H−E_1−E_2−E_3 acts by swapping coordinates 4 and 5 and toggling both, so the even signed action is compatible with the Picard marking. A rational boundary point is either on a fixed curve or at a node with its two geometric curves exchanged. A fixed form of the projective line has q+1 points over a finite field. Distinct nodes do not collide, so the reduced boundary count is f(q+1)−a+b; subtracting this from the ambient Weil–Lefschetz count gives the formula in every characteristic. The independent replay enumerated 1920 group elements and reproduced the sizes and f,a,b,t in every row. The wording 'eighteen possible polynomials' refers to eighteen type-indexed rows; they give fourteen distinct polynomials. Substitution at q=2,3,4,5 and strict positivity from q≥7 give just the two stated zeros. Both blow-up configurations are in general position on smooth conics, and direct projective-plane enumeration independently verified their empty complements. The split configuration yields the identity action; the (1)(2)(2) permutation of the five points yields +221 under the marking.
residual_risks: This is a conditional table of counts, not a classification of which Weyl types are realized over each small field.

evidence: ddff9df78fa6 calls a surface full when every rational point lies on the reduced geometric exceptional boundary. It gives q²+tau(g)q+1−m(g)(q+1)+a(g)−b(g) with tau the Picard trace and m the fixed-curve count.
The split complement count (q−5)² and split fullness iff q=5 were already recorded by Knecht–Reyes, citing Hirschfeld.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Fullness is exactly emptiness of U as a rational-point set; tau=1+t and m=f. The ostensibly different F_3 examples each consist of one rational point and two conjugate pairs on a smooth F_3-conic (five general-position points determine a unique smooth conic). On such a conic there are four rational points and three degree-two pairs. PGL2(F_3) is transitive on rational points, and the order-three subgroup of a rational-point stabilizer cycles the three pairs: it cannot fix a pair since then it would fix its two points individually, impossible for a nontrivial unipotent element. Thus it is transitive on choices of two pairs after fixing the rational point. The conic automorphisms extend through the plane embedding, so the two F_3 blow-up configurations are projectively equivalent.
